I have to echo what others have already said about Brainy. He is an absolutely brilliantly written character and his journey throughout the whole series has been both extremely enjoyable and tragic. This tale perfectly caps off the entire series and Brainy's development, while also leaving room for further stories

And this amazing character, combined with the fantastic writing and the interesting take on Wondertainment, make this an absolutely wonderful series.

It's taken me like 2 months to get through this cause I only ever get to read like one tale at a time, but these characters felt so god damn real. Everyone had their motivations, their quirks, and their believable reactions to circumstances. It's awesome to see such well fleshed-out characters on the wiki, and its equally awesome to basically see my headcanon Wondertainment (give or take a few finer details) come to life.

Excellent stuff mate

Wow. Just… Wow. What a rollercoaster!

**Spoilers!**
Close Spoilers!

Gee monetley, chrizzity, just, ah flibberdeegibbit, it's over! I'm glad that Brainy finally had his full redemption, even if the Wondertainment folks didn't neccesarily accept him.

This was really an emotional rollercoaster to read, though, especially those first few parts. But man, you really turned Brainy into a rather pleasant person compared to what he was before.

Also, one of my favorite parts about this is that Pepper finally got some more recognition. I remember reading about her in Dread & Circuses, but then we never saw her again. I suppose I was looking in the wrong place, though.

Overall, +1, your work is amazing, and I strive to have writing as good as yours!

item.content:encoded:
I am impressed by having read a truly addictive story arc whose main character
I deeply, sorely dislike.
It is a fascinating look at the inner workings of Wondertainment (tee emm)

- the niceness is nuanced and more than skin deep, but it isn't enough for everyone. Brainy consistently charges head on into every situation without thinking it through in the slightest, and despite his sorrow and regret, throws his great brainpower and massive energy into everything BUT changing himself for the better to break out of his destructive pattern.

I can't decide which was the bigger emotional climax of the tale for me: Polly finally being told, and believing, that Brian's crimes were very much not her fault although it was wrong of her to plagiarize, 3T telling Brian off for being the destructive rat he continues to be, or Icky throttling him for lying to her about his dark past. Bravo, and goddammit, now this is in my brain forever.

Brainy is probably my new favorite character and Wonder World!™ is a canon I can truly become invested in. Brainy's flaws resonate so strongly that it might as well be like looking into a mirror. The many adversities and pains he has endured throughout the series may not have made him better, but being denied forgiveness surely will. That is the strongest moment of the series and it is laid out so clearly.

Well done, DarkStuff. This has been an absolutely impressive and marvelous read. I look forward to seeing more from you.

It felt perfectly natural and expertly constructed, and all your characters — even the minor ones — felt absolutely, 100% realised. It's a shame to see it end, but I couldn't have imagined a better place to leave it. Very, very well done for constructing what is possibly one of the best tale series on the site.

item.title: The End of an Era
item.content:encoded:
I remember when the series was little more than a gleam in your eye, and you told me about it excitedly. 15 tales later, here we are. How time flies.

Brainy has never felt more raw, more real, than he does here. I feel his realization and acceptance that while his past is well and truly gone, his future is waiting for him, just one forward step away. Some things can't be forgotten or forgiven, but must be moved past. It's a fitting coda for his saga.

Godspeed, Brainy. And bravo, DarkStuff.

Bravo.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Aaaaa how do I even fucking write this author post? I just now wrote the author note at the bottom of the main hub, which says a lot of what I want it to say, but… just, I dunno. I mean, seriously, this is the end of my biggest, proudest series. Probably my biggest life achievement thus far. (Don't worry, I have plans to do bigger IRL stuff, but still!) This is closing off what has been with me for like… 9 months. It's my baby and something I have put hours upon hours into.

I guess I just have to let it be something that happened, and be happy with it.

I mean, okay, this is going to get rambly, just like our lovable protagonist, but for those not in the know, I am 16. Just gonna put that out there. And I feel like most things you write when you're 16 you're supposed to look back on later and go "ah, that was edgy, I'm glad I got past that" or "man that was dumb, I'm glad I'm a better writer now", and just… I can't see that happening. I feel like I'll always be proud of this. Like I'll always be happy that I can say I wrote a book. I mean it's over 60,000 words. A book! I can't believe it.

And of course I couldn't have done this without such a wonderful group of online friends. This is a truly gifted community. So, some shout-outs:

  • Varaxous | Was there when I was first pitching this project. Was part of the group that brainstormed the first tale. Thank you.
  • Weryllium | Was also there since the very beginning. Has been a draft reader on almost every tale, and has worked with me through the whole thing. Thank you.
  • MaliceAforethought | Another friend who's been here basically the whole time and has read everything in draft form. Thank you.
  • DrChandra | A crucial beta reader who helped me through writing in his universe of Dread & Circuses. Helped with a lot of the dialogue with Icky and Manny, helped me shape the story in general, great big help. Thank you.
  • Genshed | Seriously just calling you out for commenting so much. Comments are my bread and butter. Seeing someone invested in the series and following it helps keep me motivated. Thank you.

And to everyone else who has helped at various points in this project. Seriously, thank you all for enabling me to make something that I will be thinking about for years and years to come. You're all wonderful.

Also, DrChandra will be making a bonus article featuring Brainy Brian within a week or two, and when that goes up I will post a link to it in this very author post. Oh, what's that? It's up? Oh goody! Here it is: Somatic Backups

Thank you all for your readership!

Thank you all for making this all possible!

I love this site, and I love you guys.

Also, for sentimental value, I highly encourage readers of the series to post their thoughts in the comments here.
